failClosedGate.question: Does the hard stop actually fire?
failClosedGate.answer: Yes, on every degradation I could construct, and it fires before anything is bound.
failClosedGate.howIExercisedItWithoutBuilding: The gate lives in scripts/build-census-v1-wi_exp_cr266-set.mjs as dischargeGate(), which is not exported. I copied the committed builder verbatim into my scratchpad, rewrote only its relative import specifiers to absolute ones, appended a single line exporting dischargeGate, DISCHARGE_GATE, UNKNOWN_DISCHARGE_RECORD and FIXTURES, and confirmed by diff that the copy is otherwise byte-identical to the committed file. The builder's main guard compares process.argv[1] to its own path, so importing the copy from a probe script never calls runFamily; nothing was built and no path under the overlay directory was opened for writing.
failClosedGate.rules: matter.wi_expungement_ordered_at_sentencing must be true; matter.wi_sentence_included_probation must be false; matter.wi_sentence_included_jail_or_prison must be false; matter.wi_sentence_completed must be true. The comparison is strict identity (value === rule.mustBe), so a truthy non-boolean does not pass.
failClosedGate.probes: 18 in all. The canonical and boundary fixture records both pass. UNKNOWN_DISCHARGE_RECORD, which is the canonical record with the probation fact set to null, is refused, naming matter.wi_sentence_included_probation=null against a required false -- this is the proof PF25 says runs on every build and it does refuse. I then ran each of the four facts through four further degradations: set to null, deleted from the record entirely, inverted to the opposite boolean, and set to the truthy string "yes". All 16 are refused, each naming the offending factId, the value found and the value required. The string probe matters: "yes" is truthy and would pass a loose check, and it is refused.
failClosedGate.enforcementPoint: runFamily lines 1164-1180. gates are computed for every fixture and hardStopProof = dischargeGate(UNKNOWN_DISCHARGE_RECORD) is computed BEFORE any source is bound. If the hard stop were to pass, the build returns status STOPPED, stopClass HARD_STOP_DOES_NOT_STOP, overlayDirectoryTouched false and counters null; if any fixture fails, it returns STOPPED with stopClass DISCHARGE_TYPE_NOT_ESTABLISHED on the same terms. The stop is structural, not advisory.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.theMechanism: I reproduced it exactly. The census reader at scripts/build-census-v1-wi_exp_cr266-set.mjs lines 459-465 does `for (const stream of p.node.normalizedEntries?.().Contents?.asArray?.() ?? []) content += Buffer.from(doc.context.lookup(stream).getContents()).toString('latin1')` and passes the result straight to checkboxCandidates. It never inflates. The conclusion those records reach -- leave all eight alone, they are the court's -- is correct and independently right under Wis. Stat. § 973.015 whatever the geometry says, so no participant is harmed by the delivered page. What is wrong is that a reviewer, a counsel reader and every downstream lane is being handed a stated measurement that the repository contradicts, on precisely the controls a proposed order must never mark.
